questions.question: You need to make a Deployment in AKS reachable from the internet through a public IP address. Which Service type should you define in the manifest?

options.why: Correct. A LoadBalancer Service gets a public IP address from the Azure load balancer.
ClusterIP is reachable only from inside the cluster.
A headless Service returns pod IPs for in-cluster discovery and has no public IP.
ExternalName maps a Service to an external DNS name and does not expose pods.

questions.explanation: Use type LoadBalancer for a public IP address on AKS.

questions.question: After you apply a Deployment and a Service, the Service has no endpoints. The pods are running and ready. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The Service selector does not match the labels on the pods
options.why: Correct. A Service routes only to pods whose labels match its selector.

options.text: The Deployment has more than one replica
options.why: Multiple replicas are supported and would add endpoints.
ClusterIP Services still have endpoints for matching pods.

options.text: The image was pulled from Azure Container Registry
options.why: The image source does not affect Service endpoints.

questions.explanation: Endpoints are populated from ready pods that match the Service selector.

questions.question: Pods in an AKS cluster must pull images from the registry contosoacr without image pull secrets. Which command should you run?

options.text: az aks update --name aks-rag --resource-group rg-ai --attach-acr contosoacr
options.why: Correct. --attach-acr assigns the AcrPull role to the cluster's kubelet identity.
This enables a shared admin password, which would still require a secret.
This creates an image pull secret, which the requirement prohibits.
This configures kubectl access and does not grant registry access.

questions.explanation: Attaching the registry grants AcrPull to the kubelet identity.

questions.question: You update the image tag in a Deployment manifest and run kubectl apply. The new version causes errors. Which command should you run to return to the previous version?

options.why: Correct. rollout undo reverts the Deployment to its previous revision.
This removes the Deployment and all its pods.
This stops all pods and does not restore the previous version.
This lists events and does not change the Deployment.

questions.explanation: Deployments keep a rollout history, and rollout undo returns to the previous ReplicaSet.

questions.question: A Deployment manifest must provide an API key to a container as an environment variable. The key must not appear in the manifest. Which TWO approaches meet the requirement?

options.text: Reference a Kubernetes Secret by using valueFrom.secretKeyRef
options.why: Correct. The manifest refers to the Secret by name, not by value.

options.text: Mount the key from Azure Key Vault by using the Secrets Store CSI Driver and sync it to a Secret
options.why: Correct. The value stays in Key Vault and is exposed through the driver.

options.text: Set the env value field to the key
options.why: This places the key in the manifest.

options.text: Add the key to the image as an ENV instruction
options.why: This places the key in the image.

questions.explanation: Use secretKeyRef or the Key Vault CSI driver so the secret does not appear in the manifest or image.
